hypothesis: Corpus-derived rare two- and three-word phrases can recover the remaining missed conversation without damaging the three questions already recovered by technical-anchor search.

conditions.B: Accepted BM25 plus MiniLM plus exact technical-anchor search; five chats and up to five messages per chat.
conditions.C: The identical frozen search plus rare contiguous two- and three-word phrases generated from the question and weighted only by their frequency in the local library. No domain phrase list exists.

questions: Why did we add DeBERTa to the Pocket i harness, and why could it not be the only judge?
What relay rate limit was proposed to slow the spread of malicious messages between new recipients?
Why should passive room messages not always fail closed and ask the user for permission?
Why was the /x share feature not reachable even though its application code was already deployed?
decision: Accept C only if it exposes the needed evidence for the passive-message question and preserves the needed evidence for all other three questions. Otherwise keep the already accepted 3/4 technical-anchor result.
claim_boundary: This tests retrieval only. It does not test Qwen, DeBERTa or final answer writing.
privacy: The protocol contains no private text. Generated HTML and JSON stay on the owner's computer and are never uploaded automatically.
